resources.string: Controls a group of XPL-EX hooks. A detailed description has not yet been added for this custom or newly introduced group.

Enables one coherent device identity covering the model, Android build, CPU, GPU, SoC, memory, display, identifiers, SIM and network data. Only firmware matching the real Android version is selected; language and timezone are not changed.
Intercepts advertising and analytics services to limit usage-event collection. It can affect statistics, advertising or rewarded ads.
Replaces identifiers, device details and other data sent to advertising and analytics libraries.
Limits detection of walking, running, driving and other physical activity states.
Replaces OnePlus and OxygenOS identifiers such as security UUIDs, serial properties and vendor-specific values.
Limits access to installed and running application lists and may return empty or filtered results.
Intercepts location requests and returns the configured location or no coordinates, depending on settings.
Handles selected Appdome protection checks and can hide signs of root, modifications and analysis tools.
Hides signs of root, Xposed/LSPosed, emulation, debugging and suspicious system values.
Replaces the boot identifier normally regenerated after a device restart.
Limits identification of connected or selected keyboards and input devices.
Replaces network identifiers such as MAC, SSID and BSSID without changing the real network.
Replaces detailed LinkProperties data including interfaces, DNS servers and routes.
Replaces elapsed time since boot so uptime cannot be used as a stable fingerprint signal.
Intercepts file and stream input/output used to inspect the device environment.
Intercepts shell commands and their output to hide responses that reveal root or system modifications.
Limits access to account names and types configured on the device.
Blocks or replaces clipboard reads for the selected application.
Limits access to persistent device and user identifiers across multiple Android APIs.
Limits access to the real network state, addresses and interface details.
Limits access to synchronization accounts, adapters and status.
Limits access to mobile network, SIM, operator and telephony information.
Replaces values read from Android System, Secure and Global settings.
Replaces account lists and account details with configured or empty data.
Replaces contact-query results with empty or prepared data.
Replaces selected identifiers processed by PayPal components and may affect payment security checks.
Replaces SoC model, manufacturer, platform and related properties; values must match CPU and GPU data.
Replaces operator, network, SIM, phone-number and Telephony API data.
Replaces total/free storage capacity and selected partition information.
Intercepts analytics libraries that collect screens, actions, errors and usage duration.
Intercepts known user/device tracking used by advertising, attribution and anti-fraud systems.
Replaces Android user/profile creation time to hide the age of the current profile.
Controls the value Android reports to the selected application.
Contains related spoofing values. Changing a value does not modify the real phone; XPL-EX only reports it to the selected application.
Android system identity: OS version, build number, fingerprint and related build data. Use values from one coherent real firmware.
Controls which installed applications are visible and the reported install/update times.
Battery capacity, charge, temperature, health and cycle data. Keep all values physically plausible.
Bluetooth adapter identity and visible paired-device information. It does not switch the real Bluetooth radio.
Mobile network and cell-tower identifiers, signal data and subscription state.
Controls the clipboard content reported to the selected application.
Device model, manufacturer, brand and code names. Prefer a complete real-device profile over mixed values.
Screen resolution, density, size and refresh characteristics for the selected device profile.
Reported file creation, modification and access timestamps and related file metadata.
CPU, GPU, memory, camera, GPS and other hardware characteristics. They must match the selected model.
Reported Wi-Fi, IP, DNS, network name, MAC address and connection data.
Controls notification information visible to the selected application.
Android build properties and SystemProperties used to identify the firmware, bootloader and system state.
Values read from Android System, Secure and Global settings.
SoC model, platform, manufacturer and baseband data. Keep it consistent with CPU and GPU values.
Android ID, advertising IDs, serials, UUIDs and other identifiers used to recognize a device.
Android user/profile information such as profile creation time.
Internal XPL-EX behavior settings. Change them only when their effect is understood.
Regional values such as country, language and timezone. These remain outside automatic Spoof Device activation.
